title: Correlated file staging and deletion via ProcessGuid (Sysmon Event ID 11 / Event ID 23)
event_type: Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational channel — linked Event ID 1 (Process Create), Event ID 11 (FileCreate), and Event ID 23 (FileDelete) entries joined on ProcessGuid

callouts.explanation: The durable correlation key that ties the process-creation event to the file-create and file-delete events it later generates; the raw PID would be unreliable here since it can recycle before the delete event fires.

callouts.field_label: Event ID 11 — TargetFilename / Event ID 23 — TargetFilename
callouts.explanation: The identical path across the create and delete events establishes the create-then-delete lifecycle for one staged file, the specific pattern this subsection describes as an anti-forensics indicator.

A short interval between the Event ID 11 create time and this delete time (roughly 32 seconds here) is consistent with a payload being staged, used, and then removed shortly after execution rather than routine, unrelated file cleanup.
Only populated if the Sysmon config retains deleted-file content hashing; without it, the deleted file's identity can only be inferred from the path, not confirmed against the file that was created.

note: Illustrative and conceptual — a composite, invented example of correlated Sysmon fields for teaching purposes, not a captured screenshot of any real Event Viewer or SIEM interface.
